findings.description: The BL-504 perf test's turso arm seeds 2501 nodes via writeGraph at ~19ms/statement on the 0.7.1 turso driver — ~96.8s of the suite's 98.3s runtime is the turso seed (measured: turso arm 96784ms, walk ~15ms). The implementer scoped this out as a pre-existing adapter characteristic (test comment at :733-737), which is correct — it is not introduced by this branch — but it makes every graph-store suite run pay ~1.5min and forces a 200s test timeout. A smaller fixture would still prove RED (8.1s walk @ 651 nodes from the test's own comment already exceeds the 1s gate) while cutting the turso seed cost ~4x. Judgment call, not a defect; flagged for CI wall-clock consideration.
findings.fix_sketch: Optional: shrink fixture to ~651 nodes (keeps RED power: 8.1s >> 1000ms) or have the turso arm seed via adapter.executeMany batching once that lands (turso-adapter.ts:830 exists but writeGraph doesn't use it).

Worth a PERF backlog item: batch writeGraph's statements via executeMany or the driver's batch API. Driver version confirmed 0.7.1.
findings.fix_sketch: File PERF item: bulk-write path for turso adapter (executeMany batching in writeGraph/writeNodeBatch).

findings.description: `a.rowid - b.rowid` comparator: SQLite rowid is 64-bit; subtraction loses precision above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (2^53). Not a real risk here — node.rowid is `integer PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL` incremental from 1 (verified DDL), 2^53 rowids is unreachable for this store, and the same `a[0] - b[0]` pattern already exists in graph-store's iterative fallback (index.ts:1457). No change needed; documented for posterity.
findings.fix_sketch: None required. If rowid magnitudes ever become a concern, compare via (a.rowid > b.rowid) - (a.rowid < b.rowid).

findings.description: Comment figure '98.6s @ 2.8k nodes' is from a larger probe fixture than the test's 2501 (test comment documents 8.1s@651 -> 98.6s@~2.8k, ~12x time for 4.3x data = super-linear n^1.7). Independent RED measured 56.6s @ 2501 — consistent with the super-linear claim and the commit's 57413ms. Comment is accurate; minor variance between probe fixtures and the test fixture is expected.

The probe test's SUPERSESSION_CHAIN_SQL copy ends `ORDER BY ch.depth` while graph-store's getSupersessionChain now ends `ORDER BY ch.depth, n.rowid`, and the comment at :100-104 claims 'byte-for-byte' — now slightly stale. Probe is self-contained (separate package, not part of either branch) and its linear-chain assertion (distinct rowids per depth) still passes; purely a comment-accuracy nit if anyone reads it as a mirror of graph-store.
findings.fix_sketch: Optional future cleanup: append ', n.rowid' to the probe copy for byte-parity.
